title: Wall Street’s AI Party Is on Edge as Soaring Yields Raise Risks
key_facts: 10-year Treasury yield recently topped 5.3%; 30-year reached 5.69%, highest since 2002
Nasdaq 100 closed at a record Friday and is up 22% this year
S&P 500 is less than 1% below its August record
Q3 tech earnings per share projected to rise more than 65% (Bloomberg Intelligence); S&P 500 earnings up more than 24%
Alphabet, Amazon and Meta have seen annual free cash flow turn negative on AI spending
S&P 500 trades below 19 times projected earnings, down from over 21 in May
Some strategists see a 10-year yield near 6% as a level that could change the outlook for equities
quote_evidence: The 10-year Treasury yield US10Y recently topped 5.3% while the 30-year yield reached 5.69%, their highest levels since 2002.
Yet the Nasdaq 100 closed at a record Friday and has gained 22% this year.
why_it_matters_hint: The AI rally leans on big tech earnings to offset the cost of high interest rates.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked (403); text read in a Seeking Alpha summary on TradingView (https://www.tradingview.com/news/seekingalpha:46ffc30b2094b:0-ai-rally-defies-24-yr-high-in-treasury-yields-but-risks-are-building/). Original Bloomberg link kept as url. Note: C07-07 puts the S&P 500 near 1.9% below its high on 2 Oct close, this summary says "less than 1%" below the August record; the figures come from different outlets and dates.
